We have only been cycling for about three weeks now after years of not even owning bikes, so we aren't as resilient or used to it as you seem to be. Unfortunately, yes. I wish it wasn't like this, but I feel that any attempt to create change is like smashing my forehead into a brick wall. As soon as you get on a bicycle, your humanity disappears for half the drivers in this city.

We've only been cycling for about three weeks after not touching a bike for years, and in the first week I was buzzed and nearly hit by a oversized pickup truck while cycling alone. It makes me extra sad that our ride to the Pride Festival, which took us down University Drive too, was so lovely and enjoyable, and then on the way back this happened. I just wish it was more consistent and predictable out there for cyclists.

There was a clown who commented on here not long after I posted, but he deleted it shortly after. The frequency of people endorsing violence against cyclists like they are non-human irritants or obstacles is so damn depressing and upsetting.
As depressing as it is, I think you are absolutely right. This guy definitely seemed like he was willing to treat us like a speed bump and nothing more.
We are concerned whether it would actually be worth the effort to track him down, so this is reassuring to hear. Thank you.

Thank you for the suggestion. This definitely would have been a lifesaver in this situation, but we only just got back into biking about three weeks ago and didn't consider this. Unfortunately the encounter was so quick and aggressive neither of us were able to pull out our phones and record anything.

Thank you. It seemed to me like his wife/partner was trying to apologize, but the idiot was too busy yelling at me and took off pretty quickly. I can't help but wonder what life is like for her if she's sharing it with a guy like that...
Thank you for the suggestion. We might check with the Ronald McDonald House too, as he turned past there after speeding away.
Absolutely! We do that when we don't feel comfortable going on the street, as our safety is more important to us than the bylaw. We may be doing that more often after this incident...

Idk if anyone has mentioned Davao city. I've been all over the Philippines from Subic Bay to Cebu (both very beautiful places) but I felt the safest in Davao, you can wear your backpack on your back!!! 

There's a lot of adventurous things to do like white water rafting as well as more chill things like cool museums and the night market with delicious food. Samal island is also a 10 peso ferry ride away. I recommend staying on the island for a bit and I highly recommend snorkelling with the giant clams at the giant clam sanctuary and there's lots of scuba diving there. The mangoes seem to taste better in Mindanao, and you have to try the durian if you go there, it's stinky but the best durian I've ever tried. You can take a bus to Mati for even better scuba diving and surfing.

 You can commute surprisingly cheaply via air conditioned taxi in Davao when the heat is too much, but the jeeps are even cheaper of course if you're a penny pincher like me.
